R. Q. 1 نَأْنَأَهُ He fed him, or nourished him, well. (K.) ＝
-A2- He restrained him, or turned him back, (El-Umawee, S, K,) from a thing that he desired to do. (El-Umawee, S.) ＝
-A3- نَأْنَأَ فِى الرَّأْىِ, inf. n. نَأْنَأَةٌ and مُنَأْنَأَةٌ; [the latter an unusual form of inf. n.;] and ↓ تَنَأْنَأَ ; He was weak, (M, K,) or confused; (S;) and not firm or sound, (S, M, K,) in his judgment, or opinion. (S, M, K.) ―
-b2- نَأْنَأَ فِى الأَمْرِ He was weak in the affair. (S.) ―
-b3- نَأْنَأَ عَنْهُ, and ↓ تَنَأْنَأَ , He was unable to do it. (K.) ―
-b4- نَأْنَأَ, inf. n. نَأْنَأَةٌ; (AA;) and ↓ تَنَأْنَأَ ; (S;) He was weak, feeble, or remiss. (AA, S, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
